newsitem.title: CANADA: Value of Canadian mineral production rises in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Value of Canadian mineral production rises in 1996.

text.p: The total value of Canadian mineral production rose 13.4 percent in 1996 from its 1995 level, the federal Ministry of Natural Resources says.
Preliminary estimates show the total value of all mineral production, including mineral fuels, rose C$5.8 billion to C$49.8 billion in 1996 from C$43.4 billion in 1995, the government said.

The value of metal production declined in 1996, down C$400 million, and the value of nonmetal production also decreased, down C$200 million. The value of structural materials increased about C$70 million.
In total, non-fuel production fell about C$600 million or 3.2 percent to C$17 billion in 1996 from C$17.6 billion in 1995.
But the value of mineral fuel production rose C$6.4 billion or 24.7, offsetting the fall in non-fuel production.
The value of crude oil and equivalent increased by C$3.7 billion, natural gas by C$1.9 billion, natural gas by-products by C$700 million and coal by about C$100 million.
Non-fuel minerals accounted for 65.4 percent of the value of Canada's total mineral production.
The sharp increases were principally a result of higher prices, the government said. But volumes of the four fuel commodities recorded gains in 1996 as well.

As for metallic minerals, the volume of gold production rose 8.8 percent to 164 million kilograms in 1996. Copper production dropped 6.4 percent to 655,900 tonnes. Nickel production increased 7.2 percent to 184,500 tonnes while zinc production rose 8.5 percent to 1.2 million tonnes.
